newsitem.title: UK: Carlton, Granada in talks to buy BSkyB's BDB stake.
newsitem.headline: Carlton, Granada in talks to buy BSkyB's BDB stake.

text.p: British independent television companies Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc are negotiating to buy British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc's stake in British Digital Broadcasting, the Times newspaper said.
BDB, which is bidding for digital terrestrial television licences, is owned by the three groups.
The report in Thursday's edition said Carlton and Granada believed the satellite broadcaster's presence in the consortium could jeopardise BDB's chances of winning a licence.
The Financial Times newspaper reported on Wednesday that the Independent Television Commission watchdog had told BSkyB it must drop its holding because of fears about market domination.
BSkyB is Britain's dominant satellite broadcaster and Carlton and Granada are the two biggest independent terrestrial companies.

The ITC on Wednesday dismissed the report as speculation and said it hoped to decide by the end of June on whether to award the licences to BDB or to a rival consortium run by cable and broadcast group NTL Inc.
BSkyB shares dropped sharply on Wednesday and analysts said the threatened ITC move could loosen BSkyB's grip on British households and thwart its terrestrial ambitions.
